attributes.current: Originating from the elite Cassius recon groups, Mysticshift Duelists blend emerging scientific insights and a deepening arcane understanding, born from a world where the weave of magic is unraveling. These pioneers of martial and mystical arts integrated newfound arcane knowledge into their combat techniques, crafting a refined martial art that harmonizes elemental forces with physical prowess. Over the years, their practices spread beyond Cassius, evolving into a distinguished discipline. Today, Mysticshift Duelists are renowned warriors who embody the art of transformation, leveraging elemental stances to dynamically adapt in combat. Their path demands a profound comprehension of both the elements and one's inner self, attracting those intrigued by the challenge of mastering such versatile and potent powers.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf-y37G2KIfp8kCV40_description
attributes.current:
3rd-level Mysticshift Duelist feature

Upon embarking on the path of the Mysticshift Duelist, you commit to mastering the art of combat through both traditional weaponry and the precise application of firearms. This unique synthesis of martial disciplines forms the foundation of your journey, preparing you for the eventual creation of your signature weapon—the Elemental Gunblade.

At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one melee weapon and one firearm of your choice. These weapons become the focal point of your training, each representing one half of the duality you seek to master. Through rigorous practice, you learn to channel elemental energies into every strike and shot, laying the groundwork for the fusion of these disciplines.

Your dedication to mastering both the blade and the bullet grants you unique combat advantages. When wielding your chosen melee weapon or firearm, you gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and the attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcomming resistance.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf-y3CJaIrtowSzuyz_description
attributes.current:
3rd-level Mysticshift Duelist feature

Starting at 3rd level, you gain the ability to adopt elemental stances, each offering unique enhancements to your attacks. When you make a weapon attack, you may choose one of your stances to activate it, adding the effects from the stance if it hits. Repeated attacks made with the same stance grants additional effects stacking based on the number of successful attacks made. Switching stances resets the stacks to 0.

The saving throw DC for stance effects is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (whichever is higher).

Select two stances initially, you may choose an additional stance when you reach the 7th, 10th and 15th level in this class.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf-y3GLwZBKSIq-jgO_description
attributes.current:
7rd-level Mysticshift Duelist feature

At 7th level, you gain the ability to combine your chosen melee weapon and firearm into a singular, powerful weapon: the Elemental Gunblade. This fusion requires a ritual that spans a day and a night, during which you must channel elemental energies into the weapons, binding them with your own spirit. The resulting Elemental Gunblade is a masterwork of craftsmanship and arcane power, unique to you and unusable by anyone else.

Upon completing the ritual, you gain proficiency with your Elemental Gunblade, which retains the properties of both the original melee weapon and firearm. The elemental gunblade also counts as one of your chosen weapons and benefits from the +1 bonus to attack rolls.

Elemental Reverb[–] At 7th level, you gain the ability to instantly channel the full force of an Elemental Stance through your Gunblade. Once per short rest, as part of an attack, you can apply one of your known stance's max stack effect on your target.

Additionally, when you switch stances from max stacks, the energy release emits a 15-foot radius elemental shockwave, dealing 2d8 force damage and pushing creatures of your choice back 5 feet on a failed Dexterity save.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf-y3IsS2DGvpc68vk_description
attributes.current:
7rd-level Mysticshift Duelist feature

By 7th level, you have mastered the ability to shift between your known elemental stances in such rapid fluidity that they have begun to weave more effectively. 

As a bonus action on your turn, you enter a perfect weave state for 1 minute. If you have a stance active, you gain 5 stacks in it immediately. While in this state, when you switch to a new stance the effects from the previous one linger until the next switch. You must also switch stances every turn to keep perfect weave active. You lose perfect weave at the end of your turn if you have not switched stances atleast once. 

You may enter this state as many times as your proficiency bonus and uses recharge on a short rest

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-74SrKmSjJcXxLb_description
attributes.current:
You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take the same Fighting Style option more than once, even if you get to choose again.

Archery PHB'14 p72[–] You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.

Blind Fighting TCE p41[–] You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet. Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness. Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range, unless the creature successfully hides from you.

Defense PHB'14 p72[–] While you are wearing armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

Dueling PHB'14 p72[–] When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.

Great Weapon Fighting PHB'14 p72[–] When you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for an attack you make with a melee weapon that you are wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2. The weapon must have the two-handed or versatile property for you to gain this benefit.

Interception TCE p41[–] When a creature you can see hits a target, other than you, within 5 feet of you with an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage the target takes by 1d10 + your proficiency bonus (to a minimum of 0 damage). You must be wielding a shield or a simple or martial weapon to use this reaction.

Protection PHB'14 p72[–] When a creature you can see attacks a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must be wielding a shield.

Superior Technique TCE p41[–] You learn one maneuver of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.

Thrown Weapon Fighting TCE p42[–] You can draw a weapon that has the thrown property as part of the attack you make with the weapon.

In addition, when you hit with a ranged attack using a thrown weapon, you gain a +2 bonus to the damage roll.

Two-Weapon Fighting PHB'14 p72[–] When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.

Unarmed Fighting TCE p42[–] Your unarmed strikes can deal bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Strength modifier on a hit. If you aren't wielding any weapons or a shield when you make the attack roll, the d6 becomes a d8.

At the start of each of your turns, you can deal 1d4 bludgeoning damage to one creature grappled by you.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-76OMyCPXYW8pFt_description
attributes.current:
You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your fighter level.

You can use this feature twice, and you regain all expended uses whenever you finish a long rest. You gain more uses of this feature, as shown in the Second Wind column of the Fighter table.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-79CHEZ2qeQuxEe_description
attributes.current:
Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action.

Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-7ATCOEFQ9hoM2N_description
attributes.current:
You have a mind for tactics and getting the upper hand on and off the battlefield. Beginning at 2nd level, whenever you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself towards success.

Rather than regaining Hit Points, you roll 1d10 and add the number rolled to the ability check, potentially turning it into a success. If the check still fails, this use of Second Wind isn't expended.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-7CvOw5mRvJE1Rq_description
attributes.current:
Starting at 4th level, Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery property of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

Consult the Weapons and Weapon Masteries tables for information on masteries and their abilities.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf0-7FCoayXIIjXwOO_description
attributes.current:
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class and to four when you reach 20th level in this class.

attributes.current: at 5th level, whenever you activate your Second Wind with a bonus action, you can move up to half your speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

attributes.name: repeating_inventory_-OIf6AnRzXXgF391Yb5S_itemcontent
attributes.current: When you use your action to set it, this trap forms a saw-toothed steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center. The trap is affixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object, such as a tree or a spike driven into the ground. A creature that steps on the plate must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d4 piercing damage and stop moving. Thereafter, until the creature breaks free of the trap, its movement is limited by the length of the chain (typically 3 feet long). A creature can use its action to make a DC 13 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Each failed check deals 1 piercing damage to the trapped creature.

attributes.name: repeating_inventory_-OIf6AnTPIYNNZhZBq9Y_itemcontent
attributes.current:
If you are proficient with a gaming set, you can add your proficiency bonus to ability checks you make to play a game with that set. Each type of gaming set requires a separate proficiency.

Multiple variations of this item exist, as listed below:

- Dice Set

- Dragonchess Set

- Playing Card Set

- Three-Dragon Ante Set

See the Tool Proficiencies entry for more information.

Proficiency with a gaming set applies to one type of game, such as Three-Dragon Ante or games of chance that use dice.

Components. A gaming set has all the pieces needed to play a specific game or type of game, such as a complete deck of cards or a board and tokens.

History. Your mastery of a game includes knowledge of its history, as well as of important events it was connected to or prominent historical figures involved with it.

Insight. Playing games with someone is a good way to gain understanding of their personality, granting you a better ability to discern their lies from their truths and read their mood.

Sleight of Hand. Sleight of Hand is a useful skill for cheating at a game, as it allows you to swap pieces, palm cards, or alter a die roll. Alternatively, engrossing a target in a game by manipulating the components with dexterous movements is a great distraction for a pickpocketing attempt.

Gaming SetActivity | DC | 
Catch a player cheating | 15 | 
Gain insight into an opponent's personality | 15 |

attributes.current:
Range. A weapon that can be used to make a ranged attack has a range shown in parentheses after the ammunition or thrown property. The range lists two numbers. The first is the weapon's normal range in feet, and the second indicates the weapon's maximum range. When attacking a target beyond normal range, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. You can't attack a target beyond the weapon's long range.

Ammunition. You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack. Loading a one-handed weapon requires a free hand. At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

If you use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a melee attack, you treat the weapon as an improvised weapon. A sling must be loaded to deal any damage when used in this way.

Loading. Because of the time required to load this weapon, you can fire only one piece of ammunition from it when you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

Scattershot. When you target a medium or smaller creature with this weapon, Make an attack against all creatures within 5 feet of it at disadvantage. If targeting a larger or bigger creature, roll an additional damage die if the attack hits.

Two-Handed. This weapon requires two hands to use. This property is relevant only when you attack with the weapon, not when you simply hold it.

Heavy. Creatures that are Small or Tiny have disadvantage on attack rolls with heavy weapons. A heavy weapon's size and bulk make it too large for a Small or Tiny creature to use effectively.

Mastery: Push. Prerequisite: Heavy, Two-Handed, or Versatile Property

If you hit a creature with this weapon, you can push the creature up to 10 feet away from you horizontally if it is no more than one size larger than you.

You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits:

- On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.

- Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.

attributes.current:
Blaze Reprisal Stance	

Add 1d8 fire damage to attacks.	

Attacks ignite targets, dealing 1d8 ongoing fire damage for 1 turn.	

Create a blaze around the target, dealing 2d8 fire damage to enemies within 10 feet.	

Unleash a fiery explosion on hit, dealing 4d8 fire damage to all enemies within 30 feet. Requires a Dexterity saving throw.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf9OvT1kNj49EZnI8i_description
attributes.current:
Stone Bulwark	

Gain +2 to all saving throws and resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.	

Attacks fortify you, granting temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your Constitution modifier.	

Attacks can cause the earth to grasp enemies, reducing their speed to 0 until the end of their next turn.	

Trigger a localized earthquake, knocking enemies within 20 feet prone. Requires a Strength saving throw.

attributes.name: repeating_traits_-OIf9xQZh7yHr3Wb5z7K_description
attributes.current:
Void Embrace	

Attacks deal an additional 1d6 necrotic damage, healing you for half the amount dealt.	

Diminish enemy strength, reducing their damage output by 1d4 for 1 turn.	

Silence enemies hit, preventing them from casting spells for 1 turn. Requires a Wisdom saving throw.	

Consume life force, dealing 3d6 necrotic damage and gaining temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt. Affects all enemies within 15 feet.

attributes.name: character_appearance
attributes.current: “A lean, battle-hardened tiefling, wearing a parachute backpack, cut horns, wearing a ragged, soot-stained duster coat covered in faint arcane symbols, with mismatched goggles hanging around their neck. Their hair is singed at the edges, and they have glowing runic tattoos on their arms. They carry a large, unusual hybrid firearm—a heavy flak cannon with arcane etchings—strapped across their back.

attributes.name: allies_and_organizations
attributes.current:
General Dialogue & Quips
💬 "You see this beauty? The BDB Flak Cannon ain't just a gun—it's a statement. And that statement is 'sit down and shut up.'"

💬 "Bullets are expensive. Magic's unstable. You? You're just a problem waiting for the right solution."

💬 "Ever seen a gun that fights like a sword? No? Good. That means they won’t see me coming either."

💬 "You don’t need to outrun the zombies. You just need to run faster than the idiot next to you."

💬 "No such thing as a fair fight, only a fight you survive."

During Combat
💬 "Watch closely. I’m about to turn lead and lightning into an art form."

💬 "First shot’s a warning. Second shot’s an invitation. Third? Ain’t gonna be a third."

💬 (after blasting a zombie) "Not much left of that one—hope you weren’t attached."

💬 "Oh, you brought a knife to a gunfight? Cute. Let me show you how I do both."

💬 (lining up a shot) "Hold still. This is precision work."

💬 "Flak Shot, meet flesh. Flesh, meet the dirt."

Interacting with Survivors
💬 (leaning against a wall, inspecting the BDB) "Let me guess. You need protection, supplies, or a way out. Lucky for you, I sell all three—when the price is right."

💬 "I don’t do charity. You want in on my ammo stash? Better be bringing something useful to the table."

💬 (grinning, after a close call) "Well. That was educational. Let’s not do it again, yeah?"

💬 "Stick to the plan, and we all walk out of here. Deviate? Well… you’d better be faster than me."

💬 "I don’t trust people. But I do trust that you want to live. Let’s work with that."

When Things Go Wrong
💬 "Oh, great. More undead. Because that’s exactly what we needed today."

💬 (reloading) "Yeah, yeah, I hear the groaning. I’m working on it."

💬 "That’s a lot of zombies. That’s also a lot of potential distractions if we play this right."

💬 "Welp. Plan A just died. Time for Plans B through ‘Run Like Hell.’"

💬 (as a wall collapses) "Hah! Welp, that’s someone else’s problem now!"

One-Liners & Catchphrases
💬 "Survival’s just another business. And business is good."

💬 "Boom. Problem solved."

💬 "Nothing personal. Just numbers, angles, and opportunity."

💬 "Dead or alive? Doesn’t really matter. My gun don’t discriminate."

💬 "You only die when you run out of options. And I? I never run out of options."
